title: Why does the chapter of the Fire end by asking about your comforts?

beats.narration: This chapter marches you to the Fire. Then its final question is about your comforts. Why?
It opens with at-takathur. The piling up of increase, the race to have more. And it climbs toward the Blaze, seen with the eye of certainty.

So you brace for a question about sins. Instead it falls on an-na'im. The pleasant ease. The same word the Quran uses for the gardens of bliss. You will be stopped over your good things, not your worst.
And the design closes. The thing that diverted you is the very thing you answer for. The bounty was never a neutral hoard.
